title: Picard quotient by geometric algebraic equivalence
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a $k$-scheme, and let $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ be the group of isomorphism classes of invertible modules with tensor product as multiplication [def-sc-picard-group], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Fix the algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], form $X_{\bar k}$ by base change [def-pc-base-change], and use tensor inverse image for line modules [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $Z_X$ be the set of Picard classes whose pullbacks to $X_{\bar k}$ are algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_{X_{\bar k}}$ for the smooth-connected-family relation [def-sfb-line-algebraic-equivalence]. Define $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{\mathrm{geom}}(X)$ to be the subgroup generated by $Z_X$, and define the geometric Picard quotient to be $\operatorname{Pic}(X)/\operatorname{Pic}^0_{\mathrm{geom}}(X)$, with its natural class map. Equivalently, $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{\mathrm{geom}}(X)=Z_X$: tensoring families and dualizing them preserve geometric algebraic triviality, and the unit is geometrically algebraically trivial. No Picard scheme or representability is assumed.

source.place: I §8 and Remark 10.19 (p.50), quotient-group convention; general geometric family formulation explicitly specified in lem-sfb-semiabelian-generic-picard-class-lifting, not attributed as a verbatim Milne definition.
